14.why: Source: 'There is a bolted rap anchor at the base of the Gendarme'; stored 14 is the pitch ending at the Gendarme's base (source does not number it, matched by content)
14.text: At the foot of the Great Gendarme, where a bolted rappel anchor sits.

15.why: Source: 'Dave at the belay at the top of the first 5.9 pitch' and 'first pitch was a stellar 5.9 lieback to the top of a pillar'; matches stored 15, the Gendarme's first 5.9 pitch
15.text: On a comfortable perch on top of the pillar, once the first 5.9 Gendarme pitch is done.

1.why: P1: 'splitter crack leads straight up to a clean a bolted belay shortly below the Lithuanian lip'
1.text: At a bolted station just below the Lithuanian Lip roof.

8.why: Source P7 (numbering offset by the free variation, content matches stored 8): 'build a belay from two pitons and a small cam or two' after the overlap
8.text: On a small seat built from a couple of pitons and a cam or two.

9.why: Source P8: ends on 'sheltered, treed triangular ledge with a finger-crack anchor' after quartz and 5.6 chimneys (matches stored 9 notes)
9.text: On a sheltered, tree-dotted triangular ledge, anchored in a finger crack.

10.why: Source P9: 'You can belay at a large tree or on crack features' after the long left-facing corner and slab
10.text: At a large tree, or alternatively off nearby crack placements.

12.why: Source descent text: unrope along third-class ledges to 'a shiny bolted anchor in an alcove', from where 'two <30m raps' go to the gully; summit shoulder wording not in source, removed
12.text: At a bolted anchor in an alcove along the third-class ledges, where the rappels into the descent gully start.

1.why: P1: 'belay ledge by a pine tree'; lichen detail not seen in the fetched text, removed
1.text: On a ledge beside a pine tree.

2.why: P2: 'traverse left along a flake to a belay below a left-facing corner'

3.why: P3: 'stem right to a ledge with a large horn and a new two-bolt anchor'
3.text: On a long ledge with a big horn, at a two-bolt anchor.

5.why: P5: 'Belay just right of the Block Ceiling'
5.text: Just to the right of the Block Ceiling.

9.why: P9: 'Move the belay up and left to the high point on M&M ledge'
9.text: At the highest point of M&M Ledge, up and left of the previous stance.

10.why: P10: ends 'on a terrace below a hands crack'; 'obvious splitter wide' not in fetched P10 text, trimmed
10.text: On a small terrace beneath a hand crack.

11.why: P11: 'splitter 2-3 inch crack to a clean slab with a bolted anchor under the Hercan Roofs'
11.text: At the bolted anchor on the clean slab beneath the Hercan Roofs.

P1.why: P1: 'ledge that leads left to a belay' / 'follow it left to a good belay'; 'left end' was an inference
P1.text: At a good belay reached by following the ledge left at the top of the slabs.

P2.why: P2: 'anchor at the next crack/gully' after the steep jugs trending up and right
P2.text: At an anchor in the next major crack or gully, up and right.

P3.why: P3: 'Friable corners lead to an indistinct ledge. A fixed #1 KB is at the belay'
P3.text: On an indistinct ledge at the top of the friable corners, with a fixed knifeblade in place.

P4.why: P4: rising traverse right 'ends at a stance by some flakes, where you belay'
P4.text: At a stance beside some flakes at the end of the rising rightward traverse.

P5.why: P5: right crack at the fork 'to an uncomfortable belay with a #3 placement'
P5.text: At an uncomfortable stance in the right-hand crack past the roof, on a good #3 cam.

P6.why: P6: 'run the rope up the bordering ridge to a heathery ledge' beside the main gully
P6.text: On a heathery ledge beside the big gully, reached up the rib alongside it.

P8.why: P8: 'saddle on the ridge crest, then scramble to an anchor on the steeper wall above'
P8.text: At an anchor below the steeper wall, just above the saddle on the ridge crest.

4.why: TSA P4: 'wandering left into and across the water streak up to the next belay on a big sloping ledge'
4.text: A big sloping ledge reached after moving left across the water streak.

6.why: TSA P6: 'a great ledge on the left... the best ledge on the route'; MP: 'ledge with a two-bolt anchor. Belay there to reduce rope drag'
6.text: A ledge on the left with a two-bolt anchor, the best stance on the route and good for cutting rope drag.

1-2.why: MP P1-2: 'a two-bolt anchor at a short chimney'; 'right side of the buttress' not clearly stated, removed
1-2.text: A two-bolt station at the foot of a short chimney.

4.why: P4: 'Gain the large ledge with a dead snag, traverse left above it, and move around the corner above a live tree to the belay'; original wording shared 8 words, reworded
4.text: Above the big ledge with the dead snag, left and round a corner by a live tree.

5.why: P5: 'finish on a featured vertical face that ends at a large ledge system'
5.text: On the large ledge system at the top of the featured vertical face.

8.why: P8: 'ascend to a belay just above a large roof. Be sure to stop at the first anchor'; 'higher belay uncomfortable' unsupported, removed
8.text: Just above the large roof, at the first anchor you reach.

9.why: P9 says 'Exit left to gain a small belay stance. Do not belay here as one bolt spins'; the 'mid-face anchor' reading is not stated and the passage is ambiguous

2.why: Spokalpine P2: 'goes up past the chockstones and exits the chimney out right to a small stance'; Steph: 'behind and then over' it
2.text: At a small stance out right, after climbing behind and over the big chockstone.

4.why: Steph: 'follows the quartz dike on pitch 4, which finishes with a leftward traverse to a belay'
4.text: At the left-hand end of the traverse that follows the quartz dike.

6.why: The tree-on-a-ledge belay is attributed to Pitch 7 in Spokalpine ('We belayed at the tree on the ledge'), not 6; pitch 6 is not numbered

7.why: Steph: at the top of pitch 7 the headwall 'loomed just above' and the author built a belay with nuts
7.text: On nuts at the foot of the steep headwall.
